blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — terbutaline prolonged tocolysis boxed warning
stem: A nurse reviews an order to continue subcutaneous terbutaline as maintenance tocolysis for more than 72 hours after preterm contractions have resolved. What is the nurse’s best action?

options.A: Continue the prescription and monitor maternal pulse, glucose, and potassium during the maintenance course.
options.B: Hold the medication and clarify the prescription because prolonged or maintenance terbutaline tocolysis is not approved and carries serious maternal risk.
options.C: Arrange outpatient administration with frequent fetal monitoring so the maintenance course can continue after discharge.
options.D: Reduce the dose and continue therapy at home because lower exposure minimizes the cardiovascular risks of maintenance use.

rationale: Current terbutaline sulfate injection labeling contains a boxed warning that terbutaline has not been approved and should not be used for prolonged tocolysis beyond 48 to 72 hours, particularly for maintenance tocolysis in the outpatient or home setting. Serious maternal adverse reactions, including arrhythmias, pulmonary edema, myocardial ischemia, metabolic abnormalities, and death, have been reported. Therefore B is the safest action. Monitoring, outpatient continuation, or dose reduction does not make prolonged maintenance tocolysis an approved or label-supported use.
educational_objective: Recognize the boxed warning against prolonged terbutaline tocolysis beyond 48 to 72 hours and against outpatient or home maintenance tocolysis, and clarify such a prescription before administration.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling
source_locator: Boxed Warning — Prolonged Tocolysis; Contraindications — Prolonged Tocolysis; Pregnancy.
source_claim_supported: Terbutaline is not approved and should not be used for prolonged tocolysis beyond 48–72 hours or maintenance tocolysis in the outpatient or home setting; serious maternal adverse reactions including death have been reported.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16: evaluate appropriateness and accuracy of medication orders; review pertinent data prior to medication administration; administer medications safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all options as realistic management decisions of comparable length.
Preserved the exact boxed-warning threshold and maintenance-use restriction in the key while eliminating the original length cue.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms B uniquely follows the boxed warning. Although the key remains slightly longer because it must state both the label restriction and action, the distractors are substantively developed and no option-length heuristic reliably identifies the answer without clinical knowledge.
